Front: The Enforcement of Mediated Settlement Agreements
Back:
1. Suing on the contract
- settlement agreement is a binding contract,
- enforced outside of Singapore by either suing on the judgment

2. Consent Judgement
- register their mediated settlement agreement in court as a
consent judgment, and when necessary, enforced as a judgment, both in Singapore and internationally.

3. Registration under the Mediation Act
- Section 12 of The Mediation Act 2017 provides for certain mediated settlement agreements to be recorded as a court order. The mediation in question must fall within the Act’s definition of mediation (Section 4), be under circumstances to which the Act applies (Section 6), be administered or conducted by designated persons (Section 12(3)). Further, for the matter going to mediation, no proceedings can have been commenced. There are also various grounds under which the court can refuse to record the agreement (Section 12(4)).
- a party’s ability to stay court proceedings in favour of mediation (Section 8), and Restrictions and Exceptions to Disclosure (Section 9).

4. Arb-Med-Arb (AMA) Protocol

5. The Singapore Convention Mediation (SCM)

- Offered in collaboration with Singapore International Arbitration Centre (SIAC)
- Matter is begun as an arbitration at the SIAC and then adjourned for mediation at the SIMC- If matter settles at mediation, it is registered as an award under SIAC, and thus enforceable under the NY Convention. If it doesn’t then it goes back to arbitration where an award is obtained
- Intended to address two main concerns: –

■ Need for certainty of outcome & Ease of cross-border enforcement

- Formal Name: United Nations Convention on International Settlement Agreements Resulting from Mediation
- Opened for signing on 7th August 2019 where 46 countries signed

○ In 2020, after ratification by Singapore, Fiji, and Qatar, SCM came into force

- Provides for the cross-border enforcement of international mediated settlementagreements (IMSAs). It seeks to do for mediation what the NY Convention has for international arbitration

- Requirements for reliance:

○ A signed settlement agreement and evidence that the agreement resulted from mediation, such as mediator’s signature, a document signed by the mediator indicating mediation was carried out, and an attestation by an institution that administered the institution

- The Singapore Convention on Mediation Act (SCMA) 2020 was passed to give effect to Singapore’s obligations under the SMC

○ SCMA intended to operate in parallel with the Mediation Act

-Represent more than the ability to enforce the outcome → But is an endorsement of the benefits of mediation
